findings.summary: The two sibling ROUGH profiles disagree about the class this commit adds, and the disagreement is undocumented. CommitProtocolSimulationFlushSeqTest:56 was widened to (0.05, 0.05, 0.1, 0.05); CommitProtocolSimulationTest:25 -- the file that owns the fault model's anti-vacuity assertions -- was widened to (0.05, 0.05, 0.1, 0), so withheldPut fires in NO seed there. Its consequence is line 98: `containsExactly("ambiguousPut", "duplicatePut", "unreachable")` inside a test named aROUGHSWEEPACTUALLYINJECTSEveryFaultClassAndDRIVESFencedWritersAtTheChain. From this commit onward that green test asserts every fault class while enumerating three of four, and the only thing keeping it true is the new knob being 0. That is the exact risk FaultInjectingStore's own class javadoc names: 'a seed that silently injects nothing is a green test that proves the absence of testing'. MEASURED in a copy of the staged tree (:sequencer:test, seeds 0..29, 120 steps, 3 pods), withheldPut swept over the sim test's ROUGH: w=0 commits=175 takeovers=68 starved=1; w=0.01 commits=135 starved=2; w=0.02 commits=124 starved=3; w=0.05 commits=120 takeovers=61 starved=3; w=0.1 commits=86 starved=5. The commit loss is ~1 per injected withheld fault, i.e. mechanical rather than an amplification defect in the protocol -- so the finding is about disclosure and coverage, not about a protocol bug. Setting the sim test's ROUGH to 0.05 and updating containsExactly to four classes makes aFAULTEDSWEEPKeepsCOMMITTINGRatherThanSTALLING FAIL at CommitProtocolSimulationTest.java:172, `Expecting actual: 3 to be less than: 3`. Nothing in the diff, the added comments or the four new backlog-notes paragraphs mentions any of this.
findings.failure_scenario: Two concrete failures. (1) Today: a reader or a later agent reads the green aROUGHSWEEPACTUALLYINJECTSEveryFaultClassAndDRIVESFencedWritersAtTheChain as evidence that the sweep exercises the fault model whole, and it does not exercise withheldPut at all -- the class has zero sweep-level evidence anywhere, while the archive row for M4.13c is marked done claiming the withheld shape is now reachable by the sweep. (2) Next: whoever picks up M4.13 or M4.13d turns withheldPut on in that ROUGH and meets a red `starved` assertion at 3 against a bound of `<3` whose comment says the margin is 'measured 1 healthy and 5 with the lapse-advance removed'. The cheapest repair is isLessThan(4) -- moving a threshold in the direction that weakens its gate, non-negotiable 2, which no script enforces -- and the measurement that would tell them the bound is fine and the extra starvation is the mechanical cost of a fourth 5% class was taken by this commit's own instrument and recorded nowhere. Resolution is either (a) enable withheldPut in BOTH ROUGH profiles, update line 98 to the four classes, and record the recalibration of the starved bound with its numbers, or (b) leave it 0 in BOTH and say in the file why the class is deliberately dark until M4.13, with the measured starved=3-at-0.02 written down so the bound is never quietly relaxed. Either way the two ROUGH constants must stop disagreeing silently.

findings.summary: The round-6 note on countDraw is made incomplete by this diff. It says 'swapping the ambiguousPut and duplicatePut labels here is UNOBSERVABLE, because both streams are drawn exactly once per conditional write and neither is drawn by a read verb -- so their counts are equal in every possible workload'. withheldPut is now drawn exactly once per conditional write (putIfAbsent:240, putIfMatch:328) and by no read verb, so the unobservable-label set is three wide, not two -- confirmed by the count this diff pins at FaultInjectingStoreStreamsTest:259, ambiguousPut 4 / duplicatePut 4 / withheldPut 4. countDraw's chained ternary also now makes withheldPut the fall-through default (line 214), so a fifth stream added and forgotten there would be counted as withheldPut.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone relies on the note and assumes the new class's label is pinned by drawCounts; they swap the duplicatePut and withheldPut arms of countDraw:212-214 while refactoring, every count assertion stays green because all three totals are 4, and the only test that would catch it is eachClassIsWIREDToItsOWNStreamAndNotAliasedOntoAnothers, which the note does not name for this class. Minor because that test does cover it today.

findings.summary: Widening this file's ROUGH to include withheldPut=0.05 falsifies a measured number in the javadoc directly above the test that uses it: 'The shared-value count is this test's ANTI-VACUITY GUARD ... measured at 19 of 30 seeds.' MEASURED in a copy of the staged tree with that same 30-seed loop: seedsWithSharedValue is 20 at withheldPut=0 and 15 at withheldPut=0.05 (issued 211 -> 151, landed 175 -> 120). The 19-vs-20 gap is pre-existing drift; the drop to 15 is this diff. The assertion is only isPositive(), so nothing goes red and nothing else caught it.
findings.failure_scenario: The guard's stated headroom is what tells the next hand whether the coincidence is robust or nearly vacuous. A reader budgeting against '19 of 30' believes there are 19 seeds of margin above isPositive() when there are 15, and if a later fault class pushes it further the number in the comment keeps saying the guard is healthy while it approaches zero -- at which point the test passes for the wrong reason with a comment vouching for it.
